summary: The Fetch mathematics of sections 3.1 to 3.3 holds in its core, but four statements are false as drafted and several need conditions. The derivative of J_F is right for x > 0, constant r and W and a copy held until admission; J_F has the closed form c x - c M(s) + (c + lambda L) M(s + x), with M(t) = E[(gap - t)^+]. For a random W independent of the gap, F(x|s) becomes P(A + W <= s + r | A > s), and nothing is read before arrival iff P(W <= r) < q. Single crossing is sufficient for the threshold rule, not necessary, so the 'iff' in section 7 result 1 is false; the rule is right at every price iff F(x|s) never falls, which IFR gives. The DFR comparison is right for a proper law held until admission, and wrong with a mass at infinity: it credits c x P(G = infinity) of stall that is never incurred, and its rent term is infinite. It needs a drop time; with one, reading at the turn's end on the tool entry at lambda = 2e-5 and c = 1 gains 0.09 to 1.22 s where the draft's formula says arrival. 'Reading at the turn's end is the same as not evicting' is false: keeping beats fetching by exactly K_net S(s) - (c + lambda L) [M(s) - M(s + x)]. Fetch before arrival is empty on a falling-hazard key only for a copy that Retain itself dropped at unchanged prices; after a price fall a read at once is worth 1.6 to 2.0 s per session on the tool entry. Neither trace entry has a falling hazard everywhere (the tool model rises for 0.79 s, 24.6 % of gaps; the human model jumps up 1.44 times at its median; the 1,200 s cap is an atom), and 28.9 % of the 16,118 per-key entries the replay sent still have a rising hazard at their median. On those hints, rules that hold a staged read until admission lose 0.8 to 2.5 priced seconds per turn at lambda >= 2e-5, because 4.7 % of gaps exceed the model's p99; the same read with a drop time gains 0.3 to 0.7 s. In section 1.5 the open-queue price is (1 + Q)/(1 - rho), not 1 + Q; mu = N holds for TTFT plus decode; c is P(no other ready turn) times the cost of an empty slot-second. In section 2 recompute wins at mu = 1 and the read wins above 22 to 33 K tokens at mu = 2 with c = 1, but K_read must let the queue wait hide the lags and charge rent only while pages are held. One file changed under me: python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/next_turn_policy.py was modified at 18:23 UTC (1:23 PM ET) by someone else, adding stall_weight (default 1.0) to read_start; my runs do not pass it, and it gives the same start as dividing the rent by c in 17,366 random cases.

results.name: R1. J_F with recourse, constant W: closed form and derivative
results.statement:
Notation for all results. Time runs from now, when the session has been idle for a seconds. R is the remaining gap (arrival A = now + R); S(t) = P(R > t), F = 1 - S, h the hazard, p_inf = P(R = infinity) (session ended). M(t) = E[(R - t)^+] = integral_t^inf S(v) dv. F(x|s) = P(R <= s + x | R > s). r = seconds from releasing a read to its pages being usable (device line V + L/beta + lags). W = queue wait of the turn if its prefix is resident; D = A + W is when it is due (T in the draft). x = r - W. c = seconds of summed TTFT per second of stall; lambda = price of host memory; L tokens; lamL = lambda L; q = lamL/(c + lamL); kappa = price of a device-second; beta = device rate. Policy s: release the read at s if the turn has not arrived, else at arrival; 'arrival' is s = infinity.

Claim. Let r and W be constants with x > 0, the landed copy held until admission, costs linear, p_inf = 0. Then E[stall] = integral_s^{s+x} F(v) dv, E[early hold] = M(s + x), and
  J_F(s) = c x - c M(s) + (c + lamL) M(s + x) + kappa L/beta,   J_F(arrival) = c x + kappa L/beta.
J_F is continuous; its right derivative at every s with S(s) > 0 is
  dJ_F/ds = c [F(s+x) - F(s)] - lamL S(s+x) = S(s) [c F(x|s) - lamL (1 - F(x|s))],
and this is the two-sided derivative wherever the law has no atom at s or s + x. If p_inf > 0 and lambda > 0, J_F(s) is infinite for every finite s unless the copy is dropped at some time theta; with a drop time the derivative is unchanged for s + r < theta.
results.proof: Fix s. If R <= s the read starts at arrival and lands at A + r = D + x: stall x, no early hold. If R > s it starts at s, lands at s + r, and D = R + W, so landing - D = x - (R - s): stall (x - (R - s))^+, early hold (R - s - x)^+. So E[stall] = x F(s) + integral over u in (s, s+x] of (s + x - u) dF(u). Write s + x - u = integral_u^{s+x} dv and swap the integrals: the second term is integral_s^{s+x} (F(v) - F(s)) dv. Hence E[stall] = integral_s^{s+x} F(v) dv = x - (M(s) - M(s+x)). E[early hold] = E[(R - (s+x))^+] = M(s+x). The read is made in every case, so the device term is constant. M is convex with right derivative -S, so dJ_F/ds = c S(s) - (c + lamL) S(s+x) = c [S(s) - S(s+x)] - lamL S(s+x); dividing by S(s) gives the draft's form. An atom at s or s + x makes the left and right derivatives differ, but M, and so J_F, is continuous. With p_inf > 0, M is infinite. With a drop at theta the early hold becomes integral_{s+x}^{theta} S(v) dv - W S(theta) (result R4), whose derivative in s is again -S(s+x).

results.name: R2. J_F for a random queue wait independent of the gap
results.statement:
Let W be random, independent of R, r constant. Write Phi(s) = P(A + W <= s + r | A > s) = E_W[F((r - W)^+ | s)]: given the session is still away at s, the chance that its turn would be admitted before a read released now lands.
(B) If a read released at arrival is not re-timed: J(s) = kbar - c M(s) + (c + lamL) E_W[M(s + (r - W)^+)], with kbar = c E(r - W)^+ + lamL E(W - r)^+, and dJ/ds = S(s) [(c + lamL) Phi(s) - lamL]. The draft's rule holds with F(x|s) replaced by Phi(s).
(C) If a read released at arrival is held to its best landing (R6), at cost kstar <= kbar: J_C(s) = J(s) - (kbar - kstar) F(s).
(B) and (C) have the same best start: if P(W <= r) >= q then kstar = kbar; if P(W <= r) < q then Phi(s) <= P(W <= r) < q for all s and nothing is read before arrival. Phi is nondecreasing in s for an IFR gap and nonincreasing for a DFR gap, so R3 and R4 carry over.
results.proof: Condition on W = w and put x_w = r - w. For x_w > 0, R1 gives J_w(s) = c x_w - c M(s) + (c + lamL) M(s + x_w). For x_w <= 0: if R <= s the read at arrival lands w - r before admission (hold -x_w, no stall); if R > s the hold is R - s - x_w; so J_w(s) = lamL (-x_w) + lamL M(s). Both cases read J_w(s) = c x_w^+ + lamL (-x_w)^+ - c M(s) + (c + lamL) M(s + x_w^+). Average over W: the formula in (B). Differentiate: dJ/ds = c S(s) - (c + lamL) E_W[S(s + (r - W)^+)]. On {R > s}, R - s > (r - W)^+ iff R + W > s + r, so E_W[S(s + (r - W)^+)] = P(R > s, R + W > s + r) = S(s) (1 - Phi(s)), which gives the derivative. (C): arrivals before s cost kstar instead of kbar, a difference (kbar - kstar) F(s). The after-arrival cost c E(d + r - W)^+ + lamL E(W - d - r)^+ is convex in the delay d >= 0 with slope (c + lamL)(P(W <= r) - q) at d = 0: if P(W <= r) >= q the best delay is 0 and kstar = kbar. If P(W <= r) < q: on {R > s} the event R - s + W <= r implies W < r, so by independence Phi(s) <= P(W <= r) < q, dJ/ds < 0 everywhere, and the extra term of (C) only lowers the derivative further: arrival is best in both. Monotonicity: Phi is an average over x of F(x|s), each monotone in s in the stated direction.

results.name: R3. When the threshold rule 'start when F(x|s) >= q' is optimal
results.statement:
Let g(s) = (c + lamL)(F(x|s) - q) where S(s) > 0; by R1, J_F(s2) - J_F(s1) = integral_{s1}^{s2} S(u) g(u) du.
(i) Necessary, any law: a start s with F(x|u) < q on [s, s + e) is never optimal. The best start lies where F(x|s) >= q, or is the arrival.
(ii) Sufficient: if F(x|s) < q before some s0 and >= q after it, s0 is optimal.
(iii) Exact: with tau the first time F(x|s) >= q, the rule is optimal iff I(s) = integral_tau^s S(u)(F(x|u) - q) du >= 0 for every s > tau, the arrival included.
(iv) All prices: for continuous F(x|.), the rule is optimal for every q in (0,1) iff F(x|s) is nondecreasing in s.
(v) IFR (the cumulative hazard -ln S is convex) is the same as 'F(x|s) nondecreasing in s for every x > 0', so IFR implies (iv). With a density, d/ds F(x|s) = (1 - F(x|s)) (h(s+x) - h(s)): for a given x what matters is the hazard's change over a lag x. A mass at infinity destroys IFR (F(x|s) then falls to 0), and the first crossing must be compared with the arrival.
results.proof: (i) dJ_F/ds = S g < 0 on [s, s+e), so a slightly later start is strictly cheaper. (ii) J_F is nonincreasing before s0 and nondecreasing after. (iii) Before tau, g < 0 and J_F is nonincreasing, so no earlier start beats tau; for s > tau, J_F(s) - J_F(tau) = (c + lamL) I(s). (iv) If F(x|.) is nondecreasing it crosses every q once from below: apply (ii). Conversely take s1 < s2 with F(x|s1) > F(x|s2) and S(s2) > 0. Let m be the maximum of F(x|.) on [0, s2], first attained at u_m < s2. m < 1: if m = 1 then S(u_m + x) = 0 and F(x|u) = 1 for every later u with S(u) > 0, contradicting F(x|s2) < m. Take q = m: then tau = u_m, and on (u_m, s2] F(x|u) <= q with strict inequality near s2, so I(s2) < 0 and by (iii) the rule fails at this price. (v) F(x|s) = 1 - exp(-(Lam(s+x) - Lam(s))) with Lam = -ln S; Lam is convex iff its increments over a fixed lag are nondecreasing; differentiating gives the hazard form.

results.name: R4. Falling hazard: the optimum is at an end; exact comparison with a mass at infinity, a drop time and the device term
results.statement:
(a) If F(x|s) is nonincreasing in s from now on (true when the hazard is), J_F rises up to the last time F(x|s) >= q and falls after: the minimum is 'now' or 'arrival', never between. If the hazard is nonincreasing from age a0, 'read now beats arrival' holds on an initial interval of ages [a0, a*] and never again at the same prices.
(b) Proper law, copy held until admission: read now iff c E[min(R, x)] >= lamL E[(R - x)^+], i.e. E[min(R,x)]/E[R] >= q. The device term cancels.
(c) Any law, with a drop time: the landed copy is dropped if the session has not arrived by theta >= s + r, and a later return reads at arrival. Let K_io = kappa L/beta + lamL r_m be the fixed cost of one read (device time plus the rent of its pages for the r_m seconds it holds them before landing). The gain over reading at arrival is
  G(s, theta) = c integral_s^{s+x} [S(v) - S(theta)] dv - lamL [integral_{s+x}^{theta} S(v) dv - W S(theta)] - K_io S(theta),
where S includes the mass at infinity. Read now iff G(0, theta) > 0 for some theta. dG/ds = -dJ_F/ds; dG/dtheta = S(theta) [K_net h(theta) - lamL] with K_net = c x + K_io - lamL W.
(d) Special cases. p_inf = 0, theta = infinity: (b). p_inf > 0, theta = infinity: G = -infinity unless lambda = 0, and then read now iff c E[min(R, x); R < infinity] >= kappa (L/beta) p_inf.
results.proof: (a) dJ_F/ds = S(s) g(s) with g nonincreasing: nonnegative, then nonpositive. For the ages: let I(a) = integral_a^inf S(u) g(u) du, which is J(arrival) minus J(start at age a) up to the factor S(a). I'(a) = -S(a) g(a): I falls while g > 0 and rises after, toward I(inf) = 0, so I <= 0 once g <= 0 and {I >= 0} is an initial interval. (b) J_F(0) - J_F(inf) = -c (M(0) - M(x)) + lamL M(x), with M(0) - M(x) = E[min(R,x)], M(x) = E[(R-x)^+], M(0) = E[R]. (c) Three events. R <= s: same as the arrival policy. s < R <= theta: stall (x - (R - s))^+, early hold (R - s - x)^+, one read. R > theta: the read at s is wasted, its copy is held theta - s - r seconds, and if R < infinity the turn reads at arrival (stall x, a second read). Against arrival (stall x and one read per returning session): the stall saved is min(R - s, x) on {s < R <= theta}, with mean integral_s^{s+x} [S(v) - S(theta)] dv; the extra rent is E[(R - s - x)^+; s < R <= theta] + (theta - s - r) S(theta) = integral_{s+x}^{theta} S(v) dv - W S(theta) (use r = x + W); the extra reads are 1{R > theta}. Differentiate for the two derivatives. (d) Substitute.
results.draft_claim_checked: Section 3.3 (DFR): 'Read now iff c E[min(R, x)] >= lambda L E[(R - x)^+] + kappa (L/beta) P(G = infinity)', and section 7 result 1 'for DFR gaps the optimum is at an end'. The end-point statement is right. The formula is right for a proper law, where its last term is zero. With a mass at infinity it is wrong twice: E[min(R, x)] counts c x P(G = infinity) for sessions that never return and would cost nothing at arrival, and E[(R - x)^+] is infinite. The wasted-read probability is P(G > theta), which equals P(G = infinity) only if the copy is never dropped. J_F needs a drop time.

results.name: R5. Fetch against Retain: exact identity, hysteresis, and when Fetch before arrival is empty
results.statement:
Two policies, both measured against 'no copy from age s on, read at arrival'. keep(s, theta): a copy is in host memory at age s and stays until theta. fetch(s, theta): the copy is on the SSD; its read is released at s and the landed copy stays until theta >= s + r. With K_io and K_net as in R4:
  G_keep(s, theta) = integral_s^theta S(u) [K_net h(u) - lamL] du = K_net [S(s) - S(theta)] - lamL [M(s) - M(theta)],
and for every law and every theta
  G_keep(s, theta) - G_fetch(s, theta) = K_net S(s) - (c + lamL) [M(s) - M(s + x)]
                                       = S(s) { (c + lamL) E[(x - R_s)^+] + kappa L/beta - lamL (r - r_m) },
R_s being the remaining gap of a session still away at s.
(1) Not evicting beats reading at the turn's end by this amount; the two are not the same.
(2) If a read holds its pages for its whole duration (r_m = r), or kappa/beta >= lambda (r - r_m), the margin is >= 0: a read before arrival pays only where keeping a copy would pay. Any law.
(3) A read released at s pays iff the best G_keep(s, theta) over theta >= s + r exceeds the margin. Eviction and read-back thresholds differ by the margin.
(4) Falling hazard from the current age: Retain keeps a copy until the age u* where K_net h(u*) = lamL and never after. With c, lambda, kappa, W, r unchanged, a copy Retain dropped is never worth reading back before arrival. Fetch before arrival is non-empty on such a key only when a copy is missing although Retain would keep it: a price fell after the eviction (room freed, queue drained, device idle), or Preempt or a hard-capacity eviction took it. Then the read starts at once.
results.proof: G_keep: if s < R <= theta the kept copy saves the stall and the read (c x + K_io) and pays rent from s to admission, lamL (R - s + W); if R > theta it pays lamL (theta - s) and then behaves as the baseline. The mean is (c x + K_io - lamL W)[S(s) - S(theta)] - lamL E[min(R, theta) - s; R > s], and E[min(R, theta) - s; R > s] = integral_s^theta S = M(s) - M(theta). Writing S(s) - S(theta) = integral_s^theta S h gives the hazard form. Subtract G_fetch of R4(c), written with M as c [M(s) - M(s+x) - x S(theta)] - lamL [M(s+x) - M(theta) - W S(theta)] - K_io S(theta): every term in S(theta) and M(theta) cancels, leaving K_net S(s) - (c + lamL)[M(s) - M(s+x)]. Use M(s) - M(s+x) = S(s) E[min(R_s, x)], K_io = kappa L/beta + lamL r_m and W = r - x: per survivor, c x + kappa L/beta + lamL (r_m - W) - (c + lamL) E[min(R_s, x)] = (c + lamL) E[(x - R_s)^+] + kappa L/beta - lamL (r - r_m). (1) is s = 0. (2): G_fetch <= G_keep, so if no theta makes G_keep positive none makes G_fetch positive. (3) is the identity rearranged. (4): with a nonincreasing hazard, K_net h(u) - lamL changes sign once, from + to -, at u*; for s >= u* every G_keep(s, theta) <= 0, hence every G_fetch(s, theta) <= 0.
results.draft_claim_checked: Section 3.3 (DFR): 'Reading at the turn's end is the same as not evicting, so on such keys Fetch before arrival is empty and the decision is Retain's'. The first half is false: keeping is strictly better, by the stall of arrivals during the flight plus one read's device time. The conclusion holds under added conditions: a read is charged for its pages over its whole duration (or device time is priced), prices and W are unchanged since the drop, and Retain made the drop. It fails after a price fall or a forced eviction. Also bears on section 2: the K that Retain needs is K_net = c x + K_io - lambda L W, because a kept copy also sits in memory through the queue wait; equivalently the index's denominator should run to admission, E[min(R, h)] + W F(h|a).

results.name: R6. After arrival: where the read should land
results.statement:
With r constant and F_D the distribution of the due time D as seen at the decision, the cost c E[(l - D)^+] + lamL E[(D - l)^+] is convex in the landing l with right derivative (c + lamL)(F_D(l) - q). A read cannot land before now + r, so the best landing is l* = max(now + r, Q_D(q)), Q_D(q) the smallest l with F_D(l) >= q.
(a) Uncertain read time: the best release time is max(now, Q_{D - r}(q)), the q-quantile of the slack D - r. Only the law of D - r matters; D and r may be dependent.
(b) c = 0 gives q = 1: every landing at or after the latest possible D costs the same, including never. The rule needs a floor on c.
(c) If being late at all costs a fixed e seconds more (the wait for the next opening after the landing), the first-order condition is F_D(l) + (1 - q) e f_D(l) = q: an earlier landing.
(d) A read that cannot be re-timed once released, with an estimate of D that keeps changing: 'release at the first time P(D <= t + r | what is known at t) >= q' is never later than the best rule; it is the best rule if that probability, once above q, stays above q; otherwise it can be too early.
(e) D's law is the same for every landing because a turn whose read is in flight is passed over: its GPU turn is set by the turns ahead of it. That fails without pass-over (then a late read delays every turn behind and its lateness costs more than 1 per second), and it fails across turns: a release that lengthens the device line of a turn ahead makes that turn late, it is passed over, and this turn's D moves earlier.
results.proof: Convexity and the derivative are the newsvendor computation: d/dl of c E(l - D)^+ is c F_D(l), of lamL E(D - l)^+ is -lamL (1 - F_D(l)). The derivative is nondecreasing and changes sign at Q_D(q); on the feasible set l >= now + r the minimiser is the larger of the two. (a) With release time t the cost is c E(t - (D - r))^+ + lamL E((D - r) - t)^+: the same problem with D replaced by D - r. (b) Set c = 0. (c) Add c e P(D < l) to the cost and differentiate: (c + lamL) F_D(l) - lamL + c e f_D(l) = 0; divide by c + lamL. (d) If a rule releases at a time t where p_t = P(D <= t + r | known at t) < q, releasing dt later changes the expected cost by (c + lamL)(p_t - q) dt < 0, so that rule is not optimal; hence the best release is at or after the first time p_t >= q. If p_t then stays >= q, every further delay costs, so the first crossing is optimal (the monotone case of optimal stopping). (e) By the definition of D in section 1.3 and the admission rule of 1.4.

results.name: R7. The hazard of the trace's two gap entries
results.statement:
In the engine's model (two-piece lognormal through p10/p50/p90) neither entry has a hazard that falls everywhere.
Tool waits (0.41/1.69/16.8 s; sigma below the median 1.105, above 1.792): the hazard rises from 0 to 0.478 /s at 0.79 s idle, the 24.6th percentile, then falls; at the median it drops by the factor sigma_low/sigma_high = 0.617 (0.427 to 0.263 /s) because the two-piece density is discontinuous there; then 0.136 at 5 s, 0.058 at 16.8 s, 0.022 at 60 s.
Human waits (3.1/96/1,040 s; sigmas 2.679 and 1.859): peak 0.056 /s at 0.076 s (0.4th percentile), then falling, with a jump UP by 1.441 at the median (0.0031 to 0.0045 /s at 96 s); the 1,200 s cap carries 8.7 % of the mass as an atom, where the hazard is infinite.
For Fetch what matters is F(x|s). Tool entry: it rises only for s below 0.59 s (x = 0.5), 0.45 s (x = 1), 0.16 s (x = 2), 0.09 s (x = 6). Human entry: it also rises on [96 - x, 96] and toward the cap.
General fact: a lognormal hazard peaks at median times exp(sigma z*), where phi(z*)/(1 - Phi(z*)) - z* = sigma; the peak sits at the median exactly when sigma = 0.798, i.e. p90/p50 = 2.78. Below that the hazard is still rising at the median, above it is already falling.
results.proof: Below the median the survival function is that of lognormal(median, sigma_low), above it that of lognormal(median, sigma_high), and both equal 1/2 at the median; so the hazard is the hazard of the first below the median and of the second above. A lognormal hazard is h(t) = phi(z)/(sigma t (1 - Phi(z))), z = ln(t/median)/sigma. Setting d ln h/dt = 0 gives phi(z)/(1 - Phi(z)) = sigma + z; the left side minus z falls from +infinity to 0, so the root z* is unique, and the hazard rises before it and falls after. For sigma_high = 1.792 the peak would be at 0.081 s, below the median, so above the median the hazard only falls; for sigma_low = 1.105, z* = -0.687 and the peak is at 0.79 s. The density on each side is phi(z)/(sigma t), so at the median it jumps by sigma_low/sigma_high. The sign of dF(x|s)/ds is that of h(s+x) - h(s) (R3).

results.name: R10. Read or recompute (section 2): K_read, K_rec, the exact rule and the crossover
results.statement:
K_rec = mu gamma L is right, and the turn's own extra prefill is already in it: it is the '1' of mu = 1 + (turns delayed). It must not be added again.
K_read needs three changes. (1) The stall is c (V + lags + L/beta - W)^+, so a queue wait hides the fixed lags first. (2) The rent is lambda L r_m, with r_m the seconds the read holds its pages (from dispatch, not while parked in the device line): lambda L (lags + L/beta), quadratic in L; 1.03 s at L = 25 K and lambda = 2e-5. (3) If W can exceed r the first term is the after-arrival optimum of R6, not c E[(r - W)^+] alone.
Exact rule, linear recompute, lambda = 0: read iff mu gamma L > c (V + lags + L/beta - W)^+ + kappa L/beta. With D0 = V + lags - W:
  D0 >= 0: read iff L > L_x = c D0 / (mu gamma - (c + kappa)/beta) when mu gamma > (c + kappa)/beta; otherwise recompute at every length.
  D0 < 0: read at every length when mu gamma >= (c + kappa)/beta; otherwise read iff L < c (-D0) / ((c + kappa)/beta - mu gamma).
Per token the read is cheaper once mu > mu_x = (c + kappa)/(gamma beta).
Numbers (beta = 21.4 K tokens/s, lags 0.9 s, gamma = 0.037 to 0.044 ms, kappa = 0, lambda = 0, no device line). gamma beta = 0.79 to 0.94; mu_x = 1.26 to 1.06 at c = 1. For L = 25 K: K_rec = 0.92 to 1.10 s (mu = 1), 1.85 to 2.20 (mu = 2), 4.62 to 5.50 (mu = 5), 118 to 141 (mu = 128); K_read = 2.07 s (c = 1, W = 0), 0.62 (c = 0.3, W = 0), 0.07 (c = 1, W = 2 s), 0 (W = 5 s or c = 0). Crossover at W = 0, c = 1: mu = 1 recompute at every length; mu = 2 read above 33.0 K (gamma 0.037) or 21.8 K (0.044); mu = 5 above 6.5 K or 5.2 K; mu = 128 above 192 or 161 tokens. At c = 0.3: 11.7 K or 9.0 K (mu = 1), 4.5 K or 3.7 K (mu = 2), 1.6 K or 1.3 K (mu = 5), 57 or 48 tokens (mu = 128). With W >= 2 s, or c = 0: read at every length up to 65,536 for every mu >= 1. At saturation (c = 0) recompute would win only if kappa > mu gamma beta - lambda beta r_m, i.e. 74 to 120 TTFT-seconds per device-second at mu = 94 to 128.
mu and c move together: mu >= 2 with c = 1 means the turn behind is itself waiting on a read; if it is ready, c is near 0 and the read wins at every length. So recompute pays only into GPU time that would otherwise be idle.
results.proof: TTFT = W + S + gamma (Delta + U) (section 1.3). Recompute: the turn waits its GPU turn W, then prefills L more tokens; its own first token is gamma L later and so is every turn behind: mu gamma L with mu = 1 + turns delayed. Recompute cannot start before the GPU turn, so W hides none of it. Read: released at arrival, lands at V + lags + L/beta; the stall beyond the GPU turn is the positive part of that minus W, weighted c; it uses L/beta device-seconds and holds L tokens while in flight. Subtract: K_rec - K_read = L (mu gamma - (c + kappa)/beta) - c D0 where the read sticks out of the queue wait, and L (mu gamma - kappa/beta) where it does not; solving for the sign gives the four cases. With the rent the difference gains -lambda L (lags + L/beta) and the crossover is the root of a quadratic.
results.draft_claim_checked: Section 2: K_read = c E[(r - W)^+] + kappa L/beta + lambda L r; K_rec = mu gamma L; 'recompute wins for any length for which gamma L < lags + L/beta, i.e. always here; with one turn waiting behind (mu >= 2) the read wins for long prefixes; at saturation the read always wins'. All three verdicts hold. Refinements: 'long' at mu = 2 means above 22 to 33 K, about the mean prompt; with the rent at lambda = 2e-5 recompute wins at every length up to 65 K at mu = 2, c = 1; 'any length' holds up to the 65,536 limit on the loaded fit (crossing at 110 K) but an idle-box fit crosses near 50 K (inferred, one request above 30 K); lambda L r should count only the time pages are held.

results.name: R11. The two weights of section 1.5
results.statement:
(mu, open queue) In a first-come-first-served queue with utilisation rho, one more second of GPU work at a service start with Q turns waiting raises summed waiting by (1 + Q)/(1 - rho) seconds: the turn itself, the Q waiting, and every turn that arrives before the busy period ends. '1 + Q' leaves out the last group.
(mu, closed loop) If the extra work d shifts every user's timeline by d (GPU never idle), then sum of extra TTFT = N d - (sum of extra decode time). So mu = N is exact for TTFT plus decode; for TTFT alone it is N minus the number of running requests whose decode the extra prefill stalls.
(c) With identical requests, a stall changes the sum by exactly 0 while another ready turn is waiting to take the slot. When none is, the empty slot delays the stalled turn and every turn served later in the same busy period. So the mean cost of a stall-second is P(no other ready turn) times m, where m is the summed TTFT per empty slot-second; m = 1 only when the GPU has spare capacity.
results.proof: Open queue: extra work d at a service start raises the unfinished work by d until the busy period ends; under first come first served every turn served in that period after the injection waits d longer (to first order in d). With deterministic service tau the work present is (Q + 1) tau, the busy period lasts (Q + 1) tau/(1 - rho) more in expectation, and rho (Q + 1)/(1 - rho) turns arrive in it; total 1 + Q + rho (Q + 1)/(1 - rho) = (1 + Q)/(1 - rho). Closed loop: for one user let A_n, F_n, E_n be the arrival, first token and end of its n-th request, A_{n+1} = E_n + pause. Then the change in TTFT_n is dF_n - dA_n = dF_n - dF_{n-1} - d(decode_{n-1}); summing over n telescopes to the eventual shift of the user's timeline, d, minus the user's total change of decode time; sum over the N users. c: the admission instants are fixed by the GPU's work; while a ready turn fills each one, delaying one turn's readiness only permutes who takes which instant, and with identical requests the sum of admission times is unchanged. If an instant is left empty for I seconds, every turn served later in the busy period, the stalled one included, is I later.
results.draft_claim_checked: Section 1.5: 'In an open queue mu is about 1 + Q'; 'mean TTFT = N g - Z - decode ... so mu = N'; 'a second of stall costs c(t) = P(no other ready turn when turn i is due)'. The first is short by the factor 1/(1 - rho). The second is right for TTFT plus decode; for TTFT alone it is less (the toy gives 0.85 N; the campaigns measured 0.73 N). The third is right at both ends (about 1 with spare capacity, exactly 0 while ready work always waits) but is not a probability in between: it needs the factor m. For Fetch nothing changes in form: q = lambda L/(c + lambda L) holds with the true c, which can exceed 1.

results.name: R12. Order on the device (section 3.4)
results.statement: With every read released, earliest due date minimises the maximum lateness. With release times, preemptive earliest-due-date is a lower bound on the maximum lateness of every order; when reads cannot be interrupted, earliest-due-date among the released reads can miss a schedule that meets every due date, by at most the largest piece that cannot be interrupted. When every due date has already passed, serving in decreasing c_j / size_j minimises the sum of c_j times lateness. In between, where some reads can still be on time, the cost is weighted tardiness and neither order is optimal in general.
results.proof: The first is Jackson's exchange argument: swapping two adjacent jobs that are out of due-date order does not raise the larger of their latenesses. The second is Horn's theorem for preemptive scheduling with release times; a non-preemptible piece delays a more urgent arrival by at most its own remaining length. The third is Smith's rule: with all jobs late the cost is the sum of c_j C_j minus a constant, and an adjacent swap toward decreasing c_j/p_j lowers it. The fourth is by counterexample (enumeration below); minimising total weighted tardiness on one machine is strongly NP-hard.
results.draft_claim_checked: Section 3.4: 'Serving the released jobs in earliest-due-date order minimizes the maximum lateness ... so if any order lands every read before its turn is due, this one does. When the device cannot meet the due dates, lateness is rationed by cost per device-second'. True with preemption. The engine's dispatched reads go to one FIFO thread within a 512-page window, so the guarantee holds up to one window (about 1.8 s at 3.5 ms a page). The ratio rule is exact only when every waiting read is already late.

results.name: R13. The engine's 64-point read_start is not the minimiser of J_F in the tail
results.statement: For x = read_s - wait_s > 0 and a non-empty support, read_start never returns None ('arrival'): starting at the last support point minus x always costs at most stall_at_arrival times (count - 1)/count, 1/64 less than arrival at age 0. On a continuous falling-hazard tail the true minimiser is the arrival (R4), so the engine reports a far 'wait' where the law says 'arrival'. The plan is harmless only because remaining_gaps returns nothing once fewer than 4 points are left: for the tool entry the last points are 29.8, 39.7, 59.5, 128.7 s, so the plan dies at 29.8 s idle and the start at 125.7 s is never reached. It is not harmless at the cap: 6 of the human entry's 64 points sit at 1,200 s, so a session idle that long is staged at 1,197 s. improvements: State Fetch on the stop-loss function. J_F(s) = c x - c M(s) + (c + lambda L) M(s + x) with M(t) = E[(gap - t)^+]; the whole pre-arrival problem depends on the hint only through M, and the now-or-arrival test needs two numbers, E[min(G, x)] and E[(G - x)^+]. M is closed-form for the two-piece lognormal (m exp(sigma^2/2) Phi(sigma - z) - t (1 - Phi(z)) on each side of the median), Weibull (incomplete gamma) and exponential. Consequence for the hint format: three quantiles do not pin down E[(G - x)^+]; on the replayed hints the model understates it by 22 % (16.1 against 20.7 s) and 4.7 % of gaps exceed the model's p99. Send a capped mean or a p99 with each entry. Checked in check_derivative.py and hints_replay.py.

Make the staged copy Retain's, not Fetch's: 'Fetch = flight + keep'. G_fetch(s, theta) = G_keep(s, theta) - [K_net S(s) - (c + lambda L)(M(s) - M(s + x))], with dG/ds the Fetch condition F(x|s) = q and dG/dtheta the Retain condition K_net h(theta) = lambda L. One function gives both actions, removes the infinite rent of an ended session, and yields a hysteresis band of (c + lambda L) E[(x - R_s)^+] + kappa L/beta per session between 'worth keeping' and 'worth reading back'. On the 16,118 real hints, holding until admission loses 0.8 to 2.5 priced seconds per turn at lambda >= 2e-5 where the same read with a drop time gains 0.3 to 0.7 s. Checked in fetch_vs_retain.py and hints_replay.py.

A life-cycle statement for the paper: a host copy should exist on the ages where Retain's index is above the price; Retain acts at down-crossings, Fetch at up-crossings, a read time early. Falling hazard: keep then drop, no Fetch. Rising hazard or a sharp hint: drop at the turn's end and read back when F(x|s) = q. Example (test run of about 20 s, sigma 0.1, L = 25 K, lambda = 2e-5, x = 3 s): keeping all along costs 10.05 s, reading at arrival 3.00 s, dropping and reading back at 16.2 s costs 1.06 s. For any unimodal hazard (lognormal included) the optimum is the first up-crossing or the arrival, nothing else: 189 cases agree to 2e-6. Checked in improvements.py I2 and I6.

A one-number test of an entry's regime: a lognormal hazard still rises at the median iff sigma < 0.798, i.e. p90/p50 < 2.78; the quantile at which it peaks solves phi(z)/(1 - Phi(z)) - z = sigma (99.7 % at sigma 0.3, 87 % at 0.5, 32 % at 1.0, 4.5 % at 1.79). 28.9 % of the replayed per-key entries are on the rising side, so the paper should report both regimes per key, not one verdict for the trace. Checked in hazard_trace.py and hints_replay.py.

Closed form for a Weibull gap with shape k > 1 and scale eta: the best start solves (s + x)^k - s^k = eta^k ln(1 + lambda L/c); for k = 2, s* = eta^2 ln(1 + lambda L/c)/(2x) - x/2; for an exponential gap with mean m the rule is all or nothing, read now iff x >= m ln(1 + lambda L/c). Agrees with a grid search to 0.004 s (improvements.py I1).

Value of a hint against its sharpness. V = c x - min J_F. For a sharp hint with standard deviation d, V is about c x - (c + lambda L) d phi(z_q), z_q the normal q-quantile: each second of spread costs (c + lambda L) phi(z_q) seconds, 0.545 at q = 1/3. Exactly (lognormal, median 30 s, x = 3 s, q = 1/3): V/(c x) = 0.97, 0.73, 0.49, 0.16, 0.005 at d/x = 0.05, 0.5, 1, 2, 3.2, and 0 beyond; at q = 0.714 it is 0.41 at d/x = 0.5 and 0 from d/x = 2. Exact test that any read before arrival (held to admission) pays: sup over s of 1 - M(s + x)/M(s) > q, i.e. some start has E[min(R_s, x)]/E[R_s] > q; it matched every row. Checked in improvements.py I3.

Point forecast against distribution, exactly. A point forecast used as 'land at this time' is optimal iff it equals l* = s* + x, and l* sits at the quantile level q + (1 - q) F(s*) of the gap, which moves with lambda, L, c, r and W; so no single number is right at two prices unless the gap is deterministic, and the recourse-aware landing is never earlier than the plain q-quantile. Example (median 30 s, sigma 0.3, x = 3 s, rents 0.025 to 10 s per second): always landing at the p10 costs 0.07, 0.02, 2.8, 25, 109 s more than the optimum; at the p50 1.0, 0.4, 0.5, 9.3, 42 s; at the p90 2.2, 1.4, 0.003, 1.4, 6.8 s. Checked in improvements.py I4.

Landing quantiles on a shared device. For a fixed order the summed cost is convex in the start times, and reads that run back to back land as a block with sum over the block of (c_j + lambda L_j)(F_j(C_j) - q_j) = 0: some members land before their own quantile, some after. In a three-read example the members land at levels 0.09, 0.41, 0.75 against own q of 0.33, 0.20, 0.63, at cost 1.69 against 2.05 when each is released at its own quantile and the line pushes the later ones (17 % less). For the order when not every due date can be met, an index that falls from c_j/size_j as slack grows (apparent tardiness cost) bridges earliest-due-date and the ratio rule, which are the two limits of R12. Checked in improvements.py I5 and order_check.py.

Hybrid restore: recompute the head [0, a) on the GPU while the SSD reads the tail [a, L). Priced cost mu gamma a + c (V + lags + (L - a)/beta - W - gamma a)^+ + kappa (L - a)/beta. The best split is where the two finish together, a* = (V + lags - W + L/beta)/(gamma + 1/beta), exactly when kappa/beta <= mu gamma < c (gamma + 1/beta) + kappa/beta, i.e. mu < 2.06 to 2.26 at c = 1, kappa = 0; above that read everything, and if the lags alone exceed gamma L recompute everything. With no lags the restore rate is the sum of the two rates, 46.4 K tokens/s against 25 K and 21.4 K. At mu = 1: with 0.9 s of lags it saves 0.01 to 0.10 s at 25 K, 0.36 to 0.56 s at 46.5 K, 0.67 to 0.96 s at 65.5 K; with 0.1 s of lags (a lightly loaded box) 0.37 to 0.49 s at 25 K. Limits: the split the other way has no interior optimum (the tail's recompute must wait for the head's read); it is an after-arrival action, since the engine holds no tokens of an SSD-only prefix; and the lookup needs a host-backed anchor, which the engine-seam check must clear. Rule matched a 6,001-point search in 3,000 random cases (read_or_recompute.py).

A refill rule after a price fall. When room frees or the queue drains, read back at once the SSD-only prefixes whose keep value exceeds the margin of R5, largest value per token first; for a falling-hazard key that is 'un-evict in reverse eviction order'. Tool entry, lambda falling from 1e-4 to 1e-6: 1.7 to 2.0 s per session at ages 1 to 30 s, 0.5 s at 100 s. This is the one place where pre-arrival Fetch is non-empty on heavy-tailed keys, and it is triggered by a price change, not by idle time passing (fetch_vs_retain.py).
